question: What must handoff.md contain so a spec-driven tool can read it without knowing the plugin?
kill: a downstream reader needs plugin knowledge to use the file
head: ab83153135dc9ebd388a0676bd67abaa24c4a4f3

directions.text: fixed markdown headings with a decisions table and pointer bullets

entries.text: code: the one downstream reader on this machine (an intake tool's Decision Ledger) uses a closed provenance enum of five values: user-answered, user-delegated, codebase-derived, deferred, ticket-sourced; its table is id | decision | resolution | provenance. Our three values map 1:1 onto three of them: operator→user-answered, code→codebase-derived, open→deferred. Pointer: the installed intake-toolkit interviewing-baseline SKILL.md, section 'Provenance closed enum'.

code: render_handoff in scripts/scout.py already emits a 5-column table (id, decision, settled by, evidence, superseded by) and a version marker in an HTML comment, so a reader can detect the shape without parsing anything else.
should the handoff adopt the downstream vocabulary outright (user-answered etc.) instead of its own three words plus a mapping line?
handoff.md keeps its own three provenance words (operator, code, open) and states the mapping to ledger vocabularies in the file itself, so no reader needs the plugin

directions.learned: fixed headings plus a decisions table are enough for a human and for a ledger-style reader; the only thing missing was the vocabulary mapping, which is one line

directions.text: add a machine-readable block (YAML front matter or a JSON fence) beside the markdown

entries.text: should the handoff adopt the downstream vocabulary outright (user-answered etc.) instead of its own three words plus a mapping line? → no: own words plus a mapping line; adopting one tool's enum would make the file depend on that tool

tried: a JSON fence duplicating the decisions table. It doubles the drift surface (two renderings of one record) and the brief forbids depending on the reader; the HTML-comment version marker plus a fixed table already gives a parser a stable anchor. Not adding it.
no second machine-readable format in handoff.md; the fixed headings, the version marker and the table are the contract
whether a downstream tool should get a converter script (handoff → its ledger) ships with the plugin

directions.learned: one plain markdown file with fixed headings, a version marker and a five-column decisions table is readable by a ledger-style tool with a three-line vocabulary mapping; a second format adds drift, not readability
